title: Simplify install.sh: hardcode repo, remove dead schedule code, drop all sed
body:
## Context

Running `install.sh` on macOS fails with:
```
sed: 1: ".github/workflows/versi ...": invalid command code .
```

BSD sed requires `sed -i ''` vs GNU sed's `sed -i`. But deeper analysis shows the sed calls are either dead code (schedule substitution against templates that don't have the placeholder) or unnecessary complexity (SEMVER_REPO param for hypothetical forks).

## Acceptance Criteria

### install.sh changes
- [ ] Remove the `SEMVER_REPO` parameter — script takes only `<version>`
- [ ] Remove all schedule/cron code (lines 52-70: read/validate, lines 88-91: sed substitute) — dead code, templates have no schedule placeholder
- [ ] Remove all `sed` calls from `install_workflow()` — no substitution needed
- [ ] Update usage comment and header to reflect single-param interface
- [ ] `install_workflow()` just fetches the template, no post-processing

### Template changes
- [ ] `templates/github/workflows/install-git-semver.yml`: change `SEMVER_REPO: USER/git-semver` to `SEMVER_REPO: mangimangi/git-semver`

### README changes
- [ ] Remove `install.schedule` from config docs (line ~165, ~209)
- [ ] Remove "Runs weekly to check for updates" mention (line ~28)
- [ ] Simplify install command examples to `bash -s <version>` (drop repo param)

### Workflow changes
- [ ] Update `.github/workflows/install-git-semver.yml` (the repo's own workflow) to pass only version to install.sh (drop repo param from `bash -s` call)
- [ ] Update `.github/workflows/install-on-release.yml` if it also passes repo param

### Tests
- [ ] Add `tests/test_install.sh` (shell tests) or `tests/test_install.py` (pytest) that verify:
  - install.sh creates `.semver/git-semver`, `.semver/.version`, `.semver/config.json`
  - install.sh installs workflow templates when not present
  - install.sh skips workflow templates when already present
  - Installed workflow templates contain `mangimangi/git-semver` (not placeholder)

title: Create .semver/bump-and-release script with tests
body:
## Summary

Move all orchestration logic from `version-bump.yml` into a new `.semver/bump-and-release` Python script. The workflow currently contains ~100 lines of inline bash handling config reading, 4 conditional bump modes (push/dispatch × automerge/PR), PR creation, and release creation. All of this should live in an updatable script so the workflow can be installed once and never modified.

## Design

**Separate script** (not a git-semver subcommand) — keeps `git-semver` CI-agnostic. Follows existing pattern (`.vendored/install`, `.vendored/check`, `.dogfood/resolve`).

The script receives GitHub context via environment variables:
- `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` — "push" or "workflow_dispatch" (built-in GHA var)
- `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE` — the before SHA for push events (workflow passes this)
- `GITHUB_SHA` — current commit SHA (built-in GHA var)
- `INPUT_BUMP_TYPE` — patch/minor/major (workflow passes from inputs)
- `INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY` — optional subdir (workflow passes from inputs)
- `INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION` — optional changelog text (workflow passes from inputs)
- `GH_TOKEN` — GitHub token (set by workflow)
- `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` — owner/repo (built-in GHA var)

### Logic to move from workflow

1. **Read config** — extract `install.on_merge` and `install.automerge` from `.semver/config.json`
2. **Git user config** — set github-actions[bot] name/email
3. **Push + automerge=true** — `.semver/git-semver bump-all --since $BEFORE`
4. **Push + automerge=false** — bump-all --no-push, create PR if changes detected
5. **Dispatch + automerge=true** — `.semver/git-semver bump $TYPE [--subdir] [--description]`
6. **Dispatch + automerge=false** — bump --no-push, create PR
7. **Release creation** — iterate tags at HEAD, `gh release create` for each

### Exit behavior
- Exit 0 on success (including "nothing to bump")
- Exit 1 on error

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.semver/bump-and-release` script exists and is executable
- [ ] Handles all 4 bump modes (push/dispatch × automerge/PR) matching current workflow behavior exactly
- [ ] Handles release creation for tags at HEAD
- [ ] Reads config from `.semver/config.json` for on_merge/automerge
- [ ] Respects on_merge=false (skips push-triggered bumps)
- [ ] Sets git user config (github-actions[bot])
- [ ] New test file `tests/test_bump_and_release.py` covering:
  - Config reading (on_merge/automerge defaults and overrides)
  - Push + automerge mode (calls bump-all with --since)
  - Push + PR mode (calls bump-all --no-push, creates branch/PR when changes detected)
  - Dispatch + automerge mode (calls bump with correct args)
  - Dispatch + PR mode (calls bump --no-push, creates branch/PR)
  - Release creation (iterates tags, calls gh release create)
  - No-op when on_merge=false and event=push
- [ ] `.semver/config.json` updated: add `bump-and-release` to `files` array (triggers auto patch bump on changes)

title: Slim version-bump.yml workflow and update install.sh
body:
## Summary

Replace the logic-heavy `version-bump.yml` workflow with a thin shell that delegates to `.semver/bump-and-release`. Update `install.sh` to deliver the new script. Update the template workflow.

## Changes

### 1. `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml`
The template workflow becomes a thin shell:
- Keep: name, triggers, permissions, concurrency, checkout step, job-level `if` for skip conditions
- Replace: all inline bash steps → single step that sets env vars and calls `.semver/bump-and-release`
- The workflow passes GitHub-specific context (event.before, inputs) as env vars

### 2. `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` (this repo's own copy)
Update to match the new template. This repo dogfoods itself so both must be consistent.

### 3. `install.sh`
Add download of `bump-and-release` script alongside `git-semver`:
```bash
fetch_file "bump-and-release" ".semver/bump-and-release"
chmod +x .semver/bump-and-release
```

### 4. Vendor protection
Update `.vendored/config.json` if needed — the `.semver/**` glob already covers `.semver/bump-and-release`, so no change may be needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml` is a thin workflow (~40 lines) that calls `.semver/bump-and-release`
- [ ] `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` matches the template
- [ ] `install.sh` downloads and installs `bump-and-release` alongside `git-semver`
- [ ] Workflow passes all required env vars: `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE`, `INPUT_BUMP_TYPE`, `INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY`, `INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION`
- [ ] Built-in GHA vars (`GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_SHA`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GH_TOKEN`) are available without explicit passing
- [ ] `.vendored/config.json` protection still covers the new script (`.semver/**` glob)
- [ ] No functional regression — the new workflow + script produces identical behavior to the old workflow

title: Add _vendor self-registration to config template
body:
Follow-up to gsv-9ed5 (Vendor V2 Contract Compliance).

When install.sh creates .vendored/configs/git-semver.json on first install, it fetches templates/semver/config.json which lacks _vendor metadata. The framework needs this block for protected/allowed path enforcement.

Update templates/semver/config.json to include:

```json
"_vendor": {
  "repo": "mangimangi/git-semver",
  "install_branch": "chore/install-git-semver",
  "protected": [".vendored/pkg/git-semver/**", ".github/workflows/version-bump.yml"],
  "allowed": [".vendored/configs/git-semver.json"]
}
```

Acceptance criteria:
- templates/semver/config.json includes _vendor block with correct protected/allowed paths
- No sed/substitution needed — all values are static
- Existing repos unaffected (create-only guard in install.sh)
- Delete docs/planning/vendor-self-registration.md after implementation (knowledge migrated to issue)

title: tag --push fails when only one component bumped in monorepo
body:
In a monorepo with root + subdirectory components, 'git-semver tag --push' tries to create tags for ALL components, not just the one that was bumped. When only one component bumped, the other component's tag already exists at a prior commit and fails with 'Tag X already exists at commit Y, but HEAD is Z'.

Fix: skip tagging a component if a tag for its current VERSION already exists (at any commit). Only create tags for components whose version was actually bumped in this commit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bumping only root in a monorepo creates only the root tag, skips subdir tags
- Bumping only a subdir creates only the subdir tag, skips root tag
- bump-all that bumps both still creates both tags
- Existing tests pass, new test covers the skip-existing case

title: Git-semver files audit
body:
# Git-semver files audit

> Epic: `mdci-dev-2153` (orchestrator), per-repo plan for `git-semver`

## Problem

The `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` configuration may be missing entries for user-facing shipped files — command MDs, mode files, doc files, and other artifacts that should trigger a version bump when changed. Missing entries mean changes to these files don't bump the version, leading to stale version numbers that don't reflect actual changes.

## In scope for this repo

Audit `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` in this repo:

1. Identify all user-facing shipped files: command MDs, mode files, doc files, and any other files that end users or downstream consumers interact with
2. Compare against the current `files` entries in git-semver.json
3. Add any missing file patterns that should trigger version bumps
4. Remove any stale patterns that reference files no longer present

## Reference context (handled elsewhere)

- The same audit is being performed independently in all 6 repos (pearls, madreperla, medici, git-vendored, git-semver, git-dogfood) under this epic. Each repo's audit is self-contained.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All user-facing shipped files are covered by git-semver.json file patterns
2. No stale patterns referencing non-existent files
3. `git-semver check` passes with the updated config

## Out of scope

- Changing git-semver's behavior or configuration schema
- Adding new file types not currently shipped

## Risk notes

- Overly broad glob patterns could trigger unnecessary version bumps on non-user-facing changes. Prefer specific patterns over wildcards where practical.

title: git-semver's own pull request checks run through git-cicd
body:
Unit 2 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`), agreed with the owner on 2026-11-28. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

git-semver's pull request checks are two hand-written GitHub Actions workflows:

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` ("Tests"): on pull requests, sets up Python `3.x`, `pip install pytest pytest-cov pyyaml`, runs pytest on `tests/`. No Python version was ever chosen: `3.x` is whatever is newest, and `pyproject.toml` declares no `requires-python` at all.
- `.github/workflows/check-vendor.yml` ("Check Vendor Files"): on every pull request, `python3 .vendored/check` with full history. It is installed and protected by git-vendored.

git-cicd v0.0.3 is installed (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/`, `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` with no jobs; pull request #91), but the install delivered no `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml`: an install pull request never carries workflow files. So nothing runs through git-cicd yet.

## Required behaviour

git-semver's own pull request checks are declared as git-cicd jobs and run through it, the way git-cicd's own repository does (`mangimangi/git-cicd`: `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`, `ci/setup.sh`, `ci/test.sh`, README "The config" and "Installing").

- `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` declares an `open` job for the tests, with a setup script that installs what the suite needs on the Python floor the repository declares and a step that runs it, and an `open` job whose step is `.vendored/check`. `paths` and `needs_nothing` are chosen so documents and tracker records need no job.
- The generated workflow exists: `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate` is run and `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml` committed (it is listed as editable for the vendor check).
- No Python version is written in any workflow; `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python`, and it is the floor the tests actually pass on, found by running them on it.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` is removed.
- `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` say how the checks run here (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup`, then `check`).

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file: `check-vendor.yml`, `version-bump.yml`, `install-vendored.yml`, `dogfood.yml` and everything a manifest under `.vendored/manifests/` lists stay as they are. The vendor check runs twice for now (the old workflow and the new job); the planning session removes the old one later. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing and undo anything it reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` shows `Open / <name> / git-semver:<job>` rows for the test job and the vendor check job, `Open / Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `Open / Report / git-cicd:report`, and the commit status `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` is success. The status is a commit status, not a check run: read it from the commit's statuses.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd validate` prints `config ok: 2 jobs` (or more), and `verify` passes.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes in a clean checkout.
- The tests pass on the Python version `requires-python` names as the floor, shown by the job's setup installing that version.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` no longer exists; no other file under `.github/workflows/` except `git-cicd-open.yml` is changed.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: Coverage of git-semver and release enforced at 99%, bats for the shell scripts, and an update-vendored job
body:
Unit 8 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`), added to the plan by the owner on 2026-11-28. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

The owner, 2026-11-28: "we need 99 test coverage for all of these tool repos using bats or pytest right? these are core tooling and they need to be safe and not regress".

## What happens today

- The `test` job (`ci/setup.sh`, `ci/test.sh`) runs pytest with coverage, but `pyproject.toml` measures only one file (`[tool.coverage.run] include = ["git-semver"]`) and sets no threshold, so nothing fails when coverage drops. Measured on `main` on 2026-11-28: `git-semver` 99% of 398 statements (missing lines 624-625, 745).
- `release`, the script that bumps, tags and publishes (and that unit 4, #96, just gave a new entry point), is not in the measure at all. Its tests exist (`tests/test_bump_and_release.py`); what they cover is unknown.
- A script a test starts as a subprocess is not counted.
- The shell scripts (`install.sh`, `ci/setup.sh`, `ci/test.sh`) are not measured and have no bats tests; `tests/test_install.py` drives `install.sh` from pytest.
- This repository has no job that updates its vendored tools: `.github/workflows/install-vendored.yml` (installed by git-vendored; cron `0 9 * * 1` and a manual run with `vendor`, `version`, `private`) still does it, and is the one workflow here that git-cicd did not generate.

## Required behaviour

Coverage:

- The `test` job measures line coverage of both shipped Python scripts, `git-semver` and `release`, by name, counting runs a test starts as a subprocess, and prints the per-file report with missing lines.
- Tests are added until each of the two is at 99% or more. They exercise behaviour a consumer relies on (each case of the release decision, the protected-branch fallback, `automerge` and `on_merge`, tagging, error paths with their messages and exit codes), with `git push` and `gh` replaced at the boundary the existing tests use.
- The job fails when the total, or either file, is below 99%.
- A line is excluded only when no test can reach it, with a comment on the line saying why. A defect a new test exposes is fixed with the test that shows it and named in the pull request; any other behaviour change is out of scope.
- `install.sh` and the scripts under `ci/` have bats tests for every behaviour they have, run by the `test` job (setup installs bats) and locally through `git-cicd check`; no coverage figure is required for shell. Existing pytest tests of `install.sh` may stay.

The update job:

- `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` declares an `update-vendored` job the way git-cicd's own repository does (`mangimangi/git-cicd`: `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` and `ci/update-vendored.sh`): on `cron` `0 9 * * 1` for `main`, and by hand with `vendor` (default `all`), `version` (default `latest`) and `private` as declared inputs; its step is a script under `ci/` that runs `.vendored/install <vendor> --version <version> --pr --deps=install`, taking the inputs from `CICD_INPUT_*` and never putting them into a command line through a shell.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate` is run and the generated workflows, now including `git-cicd-cron.yml`, are committed; `verify` passes.
- `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` say how vendored tools are updated here (Actions tab, **Manual**, job `update-vendored`; the weekly schedule).

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file: `.github/workflows/install-vendored.yml` and everything a manifest under `.vendored/manifests/` lists stay as they are; the planning session removes the old workflow afterwards. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing and undo anything it reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes in a clean checkout and prints a coverage report listing `git-semver` and `release`, each at 99% or more.
- Removing a test file makes the `test` job and the verdict fail; shown once in the pull request description.
- Every exclusion carries a comment with its reason, and the pull request lists them.
- The bats tests run in the `test` job and cover `install.sh` and each `ci/` script.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd validate` reports the `update-vendored` job; `verify` passes with `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-manual.yml` and `git-cicd-cron.yml`.
- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- `install.sh`'s behaviour and `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml` are unchanged.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: An upgrade puts version-bump.yml back into a repository that removed it
body:
Unit 14 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`). Found on 2026-11-28 when the owner installed git-semver v0.1.0 into git-cicd. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

`install.sh` installs `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` whenever that file is not there (`install_workflow`, lines 77-95: "First install only ... skipped if present"). "Not there" is taken to mean "first install". It no longer does: a repository that releases through git-cicd has removed `version-bump.yml` on purpose (git-cicd, git-semver and soon git-vendored, in plan `git-dev-883c`).

Seen in git-cicd's `update-vendored` run on 2026-11-28 (run 46106498616), upgrading git-semver 0.0.15 to 0.1.0:

```
Installing git-semver v0.1.0 from mangimangi/git-semver
Installed git-semver v0.1.0
Installed .github/workflows/version-bump.yml
```

So every upgrade puts the removed workflow back on disk. Today the install pull request leaves workflow files out when it is pushed with the workflow's own token, which hides it. git-vendored now keeps workflow files in an install pull request pushed with a token that may write them (`mangimangi/git-vendored`, plan unit 5), and then an upgrade of git-semver would bring "Bump & Release" back into a repository that releases with a git-cicd job: two releases per merge, one of them pushing a bump commit to a protected branch. The file is also listed in the manifest the installer writes, so it would come back as a protected vendor file.

## Required behaviour

- An upgrade never adds `version-bump.yml`. The workflow is installed only when git-semver is being installed into a repository for the first time (no earlier git-semver install is recorded there), and only if the file is absent.
- A first install into a repository that already releases through git-cicd does not add it either: when the repository's git-cicd config declares a job whose step is git-semver's `release`, or its git-semver config sets `"bump_on": "pull_request"`, the workflow is not installed and the installer says why in one line.
- The manifest lists the workflow only when this install wrote it or it is present from an earlier install; it never lists a file that is not there.
- An existing `version-bump.yml` is left as it is, as today.
- `README.md` ("Installation", "What gets installed") states the rule: when the workflow is installed, and that a repository releasing through git-cicd does not get it.

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing. `VERSION` is raised in this change (a patch), as the `version-check` job requires for a change to `install.sh`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests (bats or pytest, no network) show: a first install into an empty repository installs the workflow; an upgrade of a repository without the workflow does not add it; a first install into a repository whose git-cicd config runs git-semver's `release` does not add it and says why; an existing workflow is untouched; the manifest never lists an absent file.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes with coverage at 99% or more and the bats tests green; `verify` passes.
- `git-semver check-bump` passes against `origin/main` (the version was raised).
- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: Raise the Python floor to 3.11; the setup tests do not depend on the host's Pythons
body:
Unit 6a of plan `git-dev-aef7` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-aef7.md`). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-28: "I think we should raise the python floor a to 3.11 but not urgent". Delivers into `plan/git-dev-aef7`.

## What happens today

`pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.10"`. That is the oldest Python the tests happened to pass on when the checks were moved onto git-cicd; nobody chose it, and it reached end of life in October 2026. `ci/setup.sh` installs the declared floor for the `test` job, so the suite, and the coverage gate, run on an unsupported Python. git-cicd, pearls and medici declare `>=3.11`.

## Required behaviour

- `requires-python = ">=3.11"`.
- The `test` job installs and runs on 3.11 (through `ci/setup.sh`, which reads the floor; no Python version is written in a workflow or in the git-cicd config) and passes, with coverage at 99% or more for every shipped Python script and the bats tests green.
- Code or tests kept only so that an older Python works are removed where a test covers the behaviour; nothing else changes in behaviour.
- `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` name the floor once and consistently.
- The version on the integration branch is already higher than `main`'s; do not raise it again for this change unless the version check asks for it. Add the changelog line if the repository keeps a changelog.

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` before finishing.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `test` job's setup output shows Python 3.11 installed and used.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes; the pull request into `plan/git-dev-aef7` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- Nothing in the repository still names `>=3.10` as the floor.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing.


## A first attempt failed in CI, and what it showed (read before starting)

An earlier attempt at this change in git-semver (`gsv-87a6`, pull request #108, closed unmerged) passed in the session container and failed in CI on five bats tests in `tests/bats/setup.bats` (tests 38 to 42 of that run: "installs the floor with uv from PATH when no interpreter is found", "installs uv into a tools venv when uv is missing too", the two "outside CI" fallbacks and "in CI, fails rather than use another Python"). pytest passed (400 tests) and coverage was 100%.

Those tests exercise what `ci/setup.sh` does when the floor Python is **not** on the machine, and they relied on the real machine not having it. With the floor at 3.10 that was true of the CI runner; with the floor at 3.11 it is not: the runner has a Python 3.11 (on `PATH` or in its tool cache), `ci/setup.sh` found it, and the "not found" paths never ran. The session container has neither, so the tests passed there.

So, in addition to the behaviour above:

- No bats test of `ci/setup.sh` may depend on which Pythons the machine running it has. Each test builds the world it describes: a `PATH` that holds only its stubs and the basic tools it needs, and the tool cache location pointed at a directory the test controls (make the location something the script reads from a variable with the real path as default, if it is fixed today). A test for "the floor is not found" must fail to find it on a machine that has every Python installed.
- Show it: run the bats suite once with a real `python3.11` on `PATH` and once without (the container), and say in the pull request that both pass.
- Check every other bats test in the repository for the same dependence on the host (interpreters, `uv`, `bats`, `gh`, `git` config) and fix what you find.

title: Adopt git-cicd 0.2.0: regenerate the workflows, declare the secrets
body:
# Adopt git-cicd 0.2.0 in git-semver: regenerate the workflows, declare the secrets

> Unit 4 of plan `git-dev-aef7` for this repository (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-aef7.md`). Delivers into `plan/git-dev-aef7`. Re-check every reference against the code before using it.

## Problem

On 2026-11-28 the owner updated the vendored tools here to git-cicd 0.2.0, git-semver 0.2.0 and git-vendored 0.0.32. The install pull requests did not regenerate this repository's workflows, so on `main`:

- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd verify` fails: "the workflows do not match the config; run: .vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate and commit .github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml, git-cicd-merge.yml, git-cicd-cron.yml, git-cicd-manual.yml". The report job of every pull request runs that comparison, so every verdict fails until the files are regenerated.
- The committed workflows are still those of git-cicd 0.0.4: a run that needs no job shows a skipped row named with raw `${{ }}` text (the owner: "I don't like that"), and the Manual workflow has two free-text fields instead of the generated form.
- From git-cicd 0.2.0 a job receives only the secrets it declares (git-cicd README, "Declared secrets and permissions"). No job here declares any, so `update-vendored` would run with the workflow's own token (its pull request then gets no checks, or cannot be opened), and the version check cannot push a missing bump.
- `ci/update-vendored.sh` and the job's `private` input still speak of `VENDOR_PAT` where the token is now `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` (`VENDOR_PAT` stays accepted as a deprecated fallback).

## What already was decided (do not reopen)

- Model: `mangimangi/git-cicd`'s own `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` and `ci/update-vendored.sh` on `main`.
- `update-vendored` declares `"secrets": ["CICD_WRITE_TOKEN", "VENDOR_PAT"]`; its script uses `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`, then `VENDOR_PAT`, then the workflow's token, and never prints a token. (If this repository's script already chooses the token another way that honours the same order, keep it.)
- `version-check` declares `"secrets": ["CICD_WRITE_TOKEN"]`, so `git-semver check-bump` can push a missing patch bump to the pull request branch (git-semver README, `check-bump`). Jobs that only check (`test`, `vendor-check`, and any other `open` job) get `"manual": false` and declare no secret.
- No job needs a `permissions` declaration here; do not add one.
- After changing the config run `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate` and commit everything it writes or removes. `git-cicd verify` must pass.
- Docs that describe these jobs, the token or the Manual workflow (README, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/`) say what is now true; a sentence such as "the job does not declare `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` yet" goes.
- No vendor-protected file is added, changed or deleted and `.vendored/install` is never run; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing. Tests never read a real token (the suite removes `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`, `CICD_READ_TOKEN`, `VENDOR_PAT`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` before every test) and never reach the network; shell changes come with bats tests; coverage stays at 99% or more.
- Run `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver check-bump --no-fix --base origin/main` and, if it asks for a bump, raise the version by a patch step with a changelog entry where this repository keeps one.

## Acceptance

- `git-cicd verify` passes; `git-cicd check --setup` passes.
- The generated Merge, Cron and Manual workflows pass `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` only to jobs that declare it; the Manual workflow has the generated form (a dropdown of jobs, named input fields).
- A run that needs no job shows the row `Nothing needed / <repo>:(nothing)`, not raw `${{ }}` text (present in the generated files).
- No text in the repository says `VENDOR_PAT` is the token to set, other than as the deprecated fallback.
